approvedHook: Your API key is hidden in .env. Why can visitors still see it?
approvedCta: Check which variables your website sends to visitors.
narration: Your API key is hidden in .env. Why can visitors still see it?
I built a Next.js example with dummy values. No real credentials or customer data were used.
One variable used the public prefix. The other stayed server only. I inspected the built browser JavaScript.
The public marker appeared in a browser file. The server marker did not appear in the browser files I checked.
In Next.js, the public prefix asks the build to include that value in code sent to visitors.
A private credential behind that public name would not stay secret. Visitors receive the browser code.
I keep private credentials on the server and send the browser only what the feature needs.
That does not replace authorization checks. Moving a key does not automatically secure a server endpoint.
So the filename is not the boundary. What matters is where the value ends up.
Check which variables your website sends to visitors.
